replacements.old: - Do not collapse Samba/CIFS batch failures into a generic Apply message when JBLibs exposes `smbHelp.lastError`. In particular, `ManagedCIFSTargetNotEmptyError` must be shown as an invariant violation with its exact target path and the safe recovery recommendation `u` -> `a`; other concrete batch exceptions should also be surfaced to the operator.
replacements.new:
- Do not collapse Samba/CIFS batch failures into a generic Apply message when JBLibs exposes `smbHelp.lastError`. In particular, `ManagedCIFSTargetNotEmptyError` must be shown as an invariant violation with its exact target path and the safe recovery recommendation `u` -> `a`; other concrete batch exceptions should also be surfaced to the operator.
- Managed mountpoint templates are root-level `mountpointTemplates`; users reference them through `mountTemplates` and keep only stable-ID overrides in `templatePoints`. Template label/path is source-of-truth and each template mount uses a stable internal ID independent of label/path.
- A newly assigned/template-added mountpoint is fail-safe `enabled=false`, `rw=false`, `my=false`; enabling and RW are explicit per-user choices. Legacy local `sftpmounts` remain backward compatible: missing `pointsSet[label].enabled` means enabled and existing RW/my defaults remain unchanged.
- Apply must resolve local + template mountpoints through JBLibs before touching the system. Disabled records stay visible/configured but are excluded from effective desired mounts, so existing physical mountpoints are removed and not recreated. Duplicate effective labels or invalid/missing templates fail closed before user mutation. Deleting or unassigning a template mount prunes its per-user stable-ID overrides so recreated access never revives implicitly.
- A template shares only the logical mountpoint definition. The effective and physical identity remains `username + point`: Samba/CIFS shares must stay per-user (`sftp_mount_<username>_<point>`) so two users can consume the same template/path with independent Disabled/RO/RW state. Do not introduce shared backing shares or persistent reference counters unless the security model is deliberately redesigned.
